html:
The Aceh War was fought between the Netherlands and the Sultanate of Aceh in north Sumatra from 1873 to about 1904. It was the longest war the Dutch fought in the East Indies.

The Dutch invaded to secure the Strait of Malacca. Their first attack failed, and after they took the sultan's palace, Acehnese leaders fought a holy war from the hills. The scholar Snouck Hurgronje advised splitting the religious leaders from the nobles.

Tens of thousands died. Women such as Cut Nyak Dhien became heroes of the resistance. Guerrilla fighting went on for years, and Aceh's sense of apartness fed later revolts against Indonesian rule, ended only after the 2004 tsunami. See Iskandar Muda.
